source.title: Fluctuation Limit of Branching Processes with Immigration and Estimation of the Means

accepted.question_text: Consider a triangular sequence of Galton-Watson branching processes with immigration X_k^(n), started from X_0^(n)=0, where the offspring mean m_n satisfies m_n = 1 + alpha/n + o(1/n), the offspring variance sigma_n^2 satisfies sigma_n^2 = beta/n + o(1/n), the immigration mean lambda_n tends to lambda, and the immigration variance b_n^2 tends to b^2. The centered martingale increments are M_k^(n)=X_k^(n)-m_n X_{k-1}^(n)-lambda_n, and the fluctuation theorem studies weak convergence of n^{-1/2}(X^(n)-E X^(n), M^(n)) in Skorokhod space. Are the Lindeberg conditions imposed separately on the normalized offspring variables (xi_{k,j}^{(n)}-m_n)/sqrt(n) and immigration variables (epsilon_k^(n)-lambda_n)/sqrt(n) necessary and sufficient for that fluctuation convergence, or can they be replaced by strictly weaker distributional assumptions?
accepted.context_brief: Optimal Lindeberg conditions for fluctuation limits

evidence.quote: Conditions (iii) and (v) are, in fact, the Lindeberg conditions for the triangular systems {ξ (n) k,j /n1/2 : n ∈ N, 1 ≤ k, j ≤ n} and {ε (n) j /n1/2 : n ∈ N, 1 ≤ j ≤ n}, respectively; see also Grimvall [4], who investigated fluctuation theorems for sequences of branching processes without immigration, and the remarks in the introduction.
This suggests that our Lindeberg-type conditions on the offspring and immigration distributions are close to being optimal.

accepted.question_text: Consider a triangular sequence of Galton-Watson branching processes with immigration X_k^(n), started from X_0^(n)=0, where m_n = 1 + alpha/n + o(1/n), sigma_n^2 = beta/n + o(1/n), lambda_n tends to lambda > 0, and b_n^2 tends to b^2. Let the conditional least-squares estimator of m_n be formed from the regression X_k^(n)=m_n X_{k-1}^(n)+lambda_n+M_k^(n) when lambda_n is known, and let the joint conditional least-squares estimators estimate (m_n, lambda_n) when both means are unknown. In the fully degenerate variance regime beta=0 and b^2=0, the normal limits obtained with the norming factors n^{3/2} for the m_n estimators and n^{1/2} for the lambda_n estimator collapse to point masses. What replacement normalization and limiting distribution, if any, describe these least-squares estimators in that degenerate regime?
accepted.context_brief: Estimator normalization in degenerate variance regime

evidence.quote: Thus, in this case, we find that n3/2(mn − mn) p−→ 0, n3/2(mn − mn) p−→ 0, and n1/2(λn − λn) p −→ 0 as n → ∞, which means that the norming factors n3/2 and n1/2 are not appropriate.
